msDesc.head: Book of hours with verses. Droitwich(?), 15th century, first half

msItem.title: Calendar
msItem.note: Notable red-letter feasts include the Translation of St Wulfstan, bishop of Worcester (7 June) and the Translation of St Richard, bishop of Chichester (16 June, fol. 3v).

Hic obiit Elinora added to the calendar for 12 March (fol. 2r), in a hand of the second half of the 15th century. The same hand adds St Edmund (fol. 2v) and the Translation of St Æthelthryth (17 October, fol. 5v).

msItem.title: Five joys of the Virgin
msItem.incipit: Gaude uirgo mater cristi qui per aurem concepisti gabrieli nuncio

msItem.title: Book of Hours
msItem.note: Leonine verses are added at each of the Hours (fols 21r–48v).
Prayers with indulgences occur at fols 65r–77v.

Includes stanzas of the Passion hymn Patris sapientia, ueritas divina (Analecta hymnica, 30, no. 13), associating successive events of Christ's Passion with the canonical hours. For discussion, see Stefan Matter, Tagzeitentexte des Mittelalters: Untersuchungen und Texte zur deutschen Gebetbuchliteratur, Liturgie und Volkssprache, 4 (Berlin, 2021).
Added suffrage to John the Evangelist (fol. 17r). Suffrage for Richard of Chichester (fols 17v–18r), immediately followed by Nicholas (fol. 18r).

msItem.title: Penitential psalms
msItem.incipit: Domine ne in furore tuo arguas me.

msItem.rubric: Quicumque hanc orationem sequentem cotidie per annum deuote deuote dixerit iniquitatem tuam sciat antequam ueniat et priusquam moriatur uidebit gloriosam uirginem mariam ad confortacionem eius.
msItem.incipit: Obsecro te sancta maria mater misericordie

msItem.rubric: Per hanc orationem sequentem quidam puer qui eam quindecim diebus ante mortem dixerat cum ad loca penarum a demonibus traheretur. per sanctum Iohannem euangelistam. mandatum gloriose uirginis marie deferentem liberari promeruit. Qui postea cuidam religioso presbitero hoc reuelauit.
msItem.incipit: O beata et intemerata et in eternum benedicta singularis atque incomparabilis uirgo dei genitrix maria

msItem.title: Office of the compassion
msItem.rubric: De compassione beate uirginis marie. ad matutinas.
In honore beate marie salutacio. cum orationibus ante .xv. psalmos dicendos

msItem.author: Bonaventure
msItem.title: Officium de passione domini
msItem.incipit: In passione domini qua salus datur lumini
msItem.explicit: desiderio retinere. Qui uiuis et regnas deus etc.
msItem.finalRubric: Expliciunt hore de passione domini edite a sancte Bonauentura apostolice sedis cardinali. Quicumque illas dixerit in honore passionis domini decem dies indulgencie habebit. Et absolutus erit ab horis canonicalibus. dum modo licitis fuit prepeditus negociis et confirmate sunt a domino pape Gregorio decimo in consilio lugdunensi.

msItem.title: Tractatus de ortu et uita sancte Frideswide et de miraculis eius
msItem.rubric: Incipit tractatus de ortu et uita sancte Frideswide. et de miraculis eius.
msItem.incipit: Prefuit australi plage Bretonum. sine neuo
msItem.explicit: Hunc tuearis chorum. pia mater seruula Cristi.
msItem.note: Partially printed in Benjamin Bossue, ‘De sancta Frideswida virgine, patrona Oxoniensi in Anglia’, in Joseph van Heck et al., eds, Acta sanctorum Octobris, Acta sanctorum, 55 (Brussels, 1853), 8.566–7.

msItem.title: Alliterative hexameter acrostic FRIDESVVITHA, on her virtues
msItem.rubric: Incipiunt uersus beate Frideswide insoliti coloris.

lg.l: Firma frideswida. fidei flos femina fida.
Rectos rite regens. regem reprobando rebellem.
Ignis iusticie iubar irradiauit in illa.
Dogmata digna dei dominabus dans duodenis.
Edibus ex eius enormes epulit estus.
Sacras sancta sibi. studuit sociare sodales.
Virgo uenusta uigens uirtutis uendicat usum.
Vt uiris uetitum uicium uitare uolebat.
Iudex iusticie iubar ingens intulit illi.
Turris tuta trucem tortorem tundere temptans.
Hic habitans humilis hostiles horruit hamos.
Angelicas acies. adamans ascendit ad astra.

msItem.note: Printed in Guido Maria Dreves, ed., Pia dictamina. Reimgebete und Leselieder des Mittelalters, Analecta hymnica medii aevi, 36 (Leipzig, 1905), 7.261 (no. 221). The first five lines also appear in the margin of London, British Library, Royal MS 11 D. i, fol. 72v.

msItem.title: Hexameter poem on Fritheswith and Æthelthryth

lg.l: ¶ Carne frideswidam genuit rex didanus iste.
Quam tibi post genuit baptismi gratia cristi.
Clara frideswidam peperit sefrida pudicam.
Quam sibi rex regum specialem iunxit amicam.
Virgo frideswida uas morum noxiua pudoris.
Coniugium regis contempsit ipse melioris.
Spreuit etheldreda terreno nubere regi.
Diuini cultus malens se subdere legi.

msItem.author: John Pecham
msItem.title: Versus de sacramento altaris
msItem.rubric: Versus compositi a fratre Iohannem de Peccham. tocius anglie primate de sacramento altaris.

lg.l: Hostia uiua uale. fidei fons gloria matris.
Donum finale. uera figura patris.
Viuens panis aue. cum numine iuncte suaue.
Me prohibens a ue. mis memor eya faue.
Manna uiatorum. uenie uia forma sophie.
Ductor amatorum. sis michi norma uie.
Panis dulcoris. celi cibus. esca saporis.
Vas saluatoris. esto memor memoris.
Presidium domine. uirtus. plebis peregrine.
Quam deus in fine. frangere neue sine.
In te pane quidem. sunt tres. non dii. deus idem.
Sunt tres non idem. non tria. numen idem.
Duplex natura. deus es hominis caro plena.
Pane manens pura. laus tibi uerbigena.
Corpus idem numero. quondam de uirgine natum.
In cruce letatum. credo uidere mero.
Panis in altari. celo caro pura. uideris.
Visu mutari. numine non poteris.
Nil eciam pateris. indignum si comedaris.
Vt uis sic caperis. hostia sponte daris.
Tu qui dignaris. tribui nobis et in esu.
Esca salutaris. mis miserere ihesu. Amen.

msItem.note: Printed in Clemens Blume and Guido Maria Dreves, eds, Hymnographi latini: Lateinische Hymnendichter des Mittelalters, vol. 2, ed. Guido Maria Dreves, Analecta hymnica medii aevi 50 (Reisland, 1907), no. 396.

msItem.author: Jean de Fécamp
msItem.title: Oratio ante missarum celebrationem dicenda
msItem.rubric: Oracio sancti Augustini dicenda a sacerdote in missa dum canitur officium. et Kyrie. Gloria in excelsis. et Credo in unum. Vel tota dicatur ante missam quod melius est.
msItem.incipit: Summe sacerdos et uere pontififex qui te optulisti deo patri

msItem.note: Added prayers, later 15th century, on fols 165r–166v.

supportDesc.collation: 12 (fols i–ii), 28 (fols 1–8), 38 (fols 9–16), 48 (fols 17–24), 58 (fols 25–32), 68 (fols 33–40), 710 (fols 41–50), 88 (fols 51–58), 98 (fols 59–66), 108 (fols 67–74), 1112 (fols 75–86), 128 (fols 87–94), 138 (fols 95–102), 148 (fols 103–110), 158 (fols 111–118), 168 (fols 119–126, no catchword, fol. 126v blank) || 178 (fols 127–134, no catchword), 188 (fols 135–142), 198 (fols 143–150), 208 (fols 151–158), 218 (fols 159–166). Catchwords at the end of most quires, some with figurative borders.

layoutDesc.layout: 23 long lines, ruled with leadpoint; written space 120 81

decoDesc.decoNote: Illuminated borders (fols 1r, 29r, 39r, 55v). Catchwords with borders, notably including ears with aures (fol. 32v), a running chicken with ut exarentur (fol. 50v), a bird with auxiliata (fol. 74v).
Illuminated initials with marginal decoration at the beginning of the main parts of the book (fols 9, 29, 39, etc.).
Rubricated, with trimmed guides, such as fol. 41r (Pächt and Alexander, 3.944).
Pricks from pouncing for copying decorations in some lower margins (e.g. fols 20, 33, 44, 46, 56, 57, 58).

binding.p: Contemporary rose-stained whittawed leather over wooden boards; space for a clasp, now missing.

origin.p: The red-letter feast of the Translation of St Wulfstan of Worcester (7 June) implies localization to Worcestershire. Van Dijk suggested an origin with Droitwich. Although he does not give a rationale, this may be deduced from the red-letter grading of the translation of Droitwich-born St Richard of Chichester (16 June) and accompanying suffrage (fols 17v–18r). The material on St Fritheswith may reflect his association with Oxford as a student.

A possible owner of the book is John Breedon, a Franscican friar of Worcester ordained in 1394, who served as parochial chaplain to the church of St Nicholas, Droitwich. For his biographical details, see Maureen Jurkowski, Were Friars Paid Salaries? Evidence from Clerical Taxation Records, in Linda Clark, ed., The Fifteenth Century, vol. 13: Exploring the Evidence: Commemoration, Administration and the Economy (Woodbridge, 2014), 136. The suffrage for Richard is immediately immediately followed by St Nicholas (fol. 18r), and a suffrage to John the Evangelist is also augmented by a marginal addition for John the Baptist (fol. 17r). Nicholas and Richard also appear together in the litany (fol. 36r). The incluson of verses by John Pecham may suggest a Franciscan connection.

history.provenance:
An erased inscription on the right pastedown reads, Iste liber bige
ie. This may be a reference to Tardebigge, 13 km from Droitwich.
James Cobbes (1602?–1685): his title page and table of contents, dated 16 January 1650 (fol. ii recto–verso).
Unidentified shelfmark, K. No. 1, 18th century (left pastedown).
